cause: The lead's own subagent and probe spend exhausted the owner's session limit (resets 16:50 KST); the rule-classification subagent died the same way. The loop kept no budget for its own Claude usage.
detail: 29 of 57 D1 sessions ended exit 1 with the account's rate-limit message, zero model turns, zero tool calls and zero answers (all of replicate 3, two A0 sessions of replicate 2, all 12 sonnet sessions). The pre-registered rule 'a crashed or timed-out session is never re-run' exists to stop outcome-dependent rerolling; these sessions have no outcome. They are moved to never-attempted/ as evidence and their slots are run once as scheduled. Criterion is mechanical and outcome-blind: ended != exit 0 AND num_turns is None AND no answers AND no tool calls AND result text contains 'session limit'. Any session that produced a model turn stays as it ended.
title: D1 protocol amendment, made before any score was read: a session the provider refused before its first turn is never-attempted, not failed

detail: L0020's criterion matched nothing because the CLI reports num_turns = 1 for a request the provider refused. L0020 stands as written; its never_attempted list is empty because its criterion was wrong.
title: Correction to L0020: the never-attempted criterion is 'no tokens billed', not 'num_turns is None'

detail: These sessions made model turns and tool calls and were then cut off by the same provider limit before emitting any answer. Scoring them as wrong would charge an environment failure to the model, and three of four are arm A0, so it would bias the floor test. Criterion, outcome-blind: ended != exit 0 AND no answers AND result text is the provider's limit message. They are kept under interrupted/ and their slots run once. One pass only: a slot that fails again stays missing and resolves its events on what exists. Session-mean metrics use completed sessions only.
